description:
Bridgeport Family Dental Center is your family dentist in Bridgeport, Chicago, IL. At our dental office, we create a comfortable, friendly environment and our staff is fully trained and prepared to handle any dental care needs.

Our patients agree we are the best dentist in the Chicago area and we love what we do! We are proud to offer a full range of dental services, including preventive dental care and extensive restorative dentistry. No dental need is too great or too small for our knowledgeable staff.

We proudly serve the Chicago and Bridgeport area. However, because of our friendly, comfortable atmosphere and high quality dental services, we also have returning patients from as far away as out of state. Give us a call today!

Bite down gently on the gauze provided. Avoid spitting forcefully, rinsing with pressure, or using a straw — these create suction that can dislodge the blood clot and lead to dry socket. Keep your head elevated and rest as much as possible.
Some swelling, mild soreness, and light bleeding are all normal during this window. The clot forming in the socket is doing essential work protecting the underlying tissue and bone.

[{"id": "8642801929224370405", "text": "When only one tooth is missing—especially one that isn’t easily visible—it can be tempting to leave the space alone. However, every tooth contributes to a balanced bite, comfortable chewing, and the stability of the surrounding teeth. A single-tooth dental implant replaces both the visible tooth and the root beneath it, helping preserve the area without relying on neighboring teeth for support. At DentArt Chicago, we help patients consider the long-term effects of tooth loss so they can decide whether an implant is the right investment in their oral health.

Why Replacing a Single Missing Tooth Matters
A single missing tooth may seem like an isolated concern, but the teeth, jawbone, and bite all work together as one system. When one part is missing, the surrounding structures gradually adapt to the open space. Replacing the tooth can help prevent these changes and maintain more balanced oral function over time.

What Happens If a Single Missing Tooth Is Ignored?
Without a tooth root to stimulate it, the jawbone within the empty space can gradually lose volume. Neighboring teeth may also begin to tilt or drift toward the gap, while the tooth above or below it may move because it no longer meets resistance when you bite.

As these changes progress, pressure may no longer be distributed evenly across your teeth. Either way, it comes from what we see in you, tooth by tooth.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNjms3Ut4nSoZeg4wvIAxZYoHKKES8RxH-BC44=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-06-24T13:57:17", "expires_at": "2026-12-24T13:57:15", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "9112521629353775414", "text": "At Ganger Family Dentistry in Chicago, a hygiene visit is more than a cleaning. Our hygiene team focuses on your preventive health and gum care, watching for the early signs that are easy to miss and working alongside Dr. Ganger to catch problems while they're still simple to treat.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNEP52dHgm5SoBAGDhUoj2Hyb8Fnw0foNprf0w=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-06-17T13:40:06", "expires_at": "2026-12-17T13:40:06", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6619457994552462210", "text": "In a world where dental chains push patients through like an assembly line, here's what makes things different at Ganger Family Dentistry...

Dr. Urvi Ganger has a personal rule: she doesn't leave the room until you truly understand what's going on with your smile.

Not when the timer runs out. Not when the schedule says it's time. Not when the next patient is waiting. She leaves when you feel ready.

That means sitting with you until every question is answered. Re-explaining things as many times as you need, with zero judgment. Making sure every recommendation feels right to you before you ever talk numbers.

This is what independent, heart-centered dentistry looks like. No corporate quotas. No rushed conversations. No "we'll explain at your next visit." Just real care from a real dentist who actually has the time to listen.

We hear it from new patients every week — "I've never had a dentist explain things to me like this before." That feedback makes us both sad and proud. Sad that it's rare. Proud that we get to be different.

You deserve a dental home that values you over the numbers. A team that sees you as a whole person, not a procedure code.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNVef21TI-LPPHro3JsYb26VmqcYR6JrTtY3Mg=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-06-10T13:08:03", "expires_at": "2026-12-10T13:08:02", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "483308076554649798", "text": ""What's this going to cost me?"

If you've ever delayed dental care because you were afraid of the price tag, you're not alone. It's one of the most common questions we hear — and we're never offended by it.

Here's how we handle the financial side...

Dr. Urvi Ganger focuses on your smile and clinical care. Her husband Milan focuses on the financial journey. He genuinely understands the ins and outs of dental insurance, and he uses that knowledge to work for you.

When you sit down with Milan, he listens to what matters most to you. He walks you through your treatment step by step. He looks at your benefits and figures out how to maximize every dollar. He helps prioritize what's urgent versus what can wait. And he builds a plan that works backwards from your actual budget.

No pressure. No surprises. No feeling rushed into decisions you're not ready for.

We know the financial conversation can feel scary — sometimes scarier than the dental work itself. That's exactly why we slow down and walk through every detail with you. Because you deserve a dental home that protects your health and respects your wallet.

Your priorities matter here.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMHiWnn0JrhfrgeYvdKHDckUwhNuEWrcwWBznM=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-06-03T00:00:00", "expires_at": "2026-12-02T14:19:06", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1700823068420608117", "text": "What looks effortless when you're in the dental chair is actually a whole choreography happening behind the scenes.

Our team had a fun realization this week — the day-to-day rhythm of our practice could practically be set to music. There's a constant, coordinated motion that patients rarely see: moving between operatories to keep every patient on schedule, shifting into hygiene mode the moment a chair is ready, leaning over patients with dental loupes for precision focus, and working through treatment plans, insurance coordination, and aligner check-ins all before lunch. Add in digital scans and X-rays for every comprehensive exam, and it's a full day of synchronized teamwork.

Even the physical side is real. Dental work is far more demanding than most people realize — our hygienist, Pam, stretches between cleanings because hours of careful, detailed work takes a genuine toll on the body. It's a reminder of how much physical care goes into every gentle cleaning.

Here's why this matters for you: when a team knows each other's rhythm, anticipates each other's needs, and keeps everything moving smoothly, your appointment feels calm and unhurried. The behind-the-scenes hustle is exactly what creates a peaceful, unrushed experience in the chair.

That's the difference an independent, family-run practice can offer — a team that has worked together for years, moving in sync so your time with us feels relaxed and personal.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPM5RRLP0a5ADIPJB0rWGvmVFaRxkgP9wv5Osc=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-05-27T13:39:38", "expires_at": "2026-11-26T13:39:36", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2522094212681957523", "text": "Why don't we rush you through your appointment?

Because we don't have to.

Here at Ganger Family Dentistry, we don't have production goals. We don't have quotas. We don't answer to shareholders or corporate executives sitting in some office hundreds of miles away.

We're a privately owned, independent dental practice in the heart of City — and we're proud of that.

What does that actually mean for you?

It means Dr. Urvi Ganger spends as much time as you need — not as much as a corporate schedule allows. It means we explain your treatment until you genuinely understand it, even if that takes an extra 20 minutes. It means our recommendations are based on what's best for your health, not what's best for someone else's bottom line. And it means when you reach out, you connect with people who know your name, your story, and your family.

You're not a number here. You're not a "case." You're a neighbor, a friend, someone we genuinely care about helping.

This is what dentistry looks like when patients come first — not profits. From comprehensive family dentistry to orthodontics and Invisalign, every aspect of our care is shaped by the freedom that independent practice gives us — the freedom to slow down, listen, and treat you the way we'd treat our own family.

Serving the community for over 8 years.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNWtuI44NJn38OW_EXKB6FLxD-zFDRfXY1khj4=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-05-20T13:16:29", "expires_at": "2026-11-19T13:16:28", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7219757187910207054", "text": "Every dental office has that one coworker — the one everyone calls when something's on the top shelf, the ceiling tile is crooked, or the supplies are just out of reach. We're grateful for ours.

But here's something we've come to deeply believe at our dental practice: the energy a team has behind the scenes shows up in every single patient interaction.

When team members genuinely enjoy working with each other — the inside jokes, the laughs between appointments, the years of working side by side — that warmth carries straight through to the families who walk through our doors.

You can feel it the moment you arrive at our office. The front desk greets you by name. Your hygienist remembers your sensitive spots from last visit. Dr. Ganger takes the time to actually explain what's happening in your mouth, never rushing, never treating appointments like an assembly line.

This kind of consistency only happens when a dental team has stayed together for years. It's why we can track subtle changes in your oral health over time, coordinate your treatment plan thoughtfully, and remember the small things that make your visits comfortable.

Real connection between teammates becomes real connection with patients. Your dental home should feel like a place where people genuinely know you — not somewhere you're processed through. For families looking for that kind of care, that's exactly what we work to be every single day.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNLm61CYZ-gIYW8BouN6U2FHTnArUPmEtHYy_c=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-05-13T13:13:12", "expires_at": "2026-11-12T13:13:10", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2870388252397219911", "text": "There's a moment in our office that we love watching — when a patient sees their own mouth on the screen for the first time.

We've invested in facial scanners, 3D imaging, and CBCT technology. But the value isn't in the tools themselves. It's in what they let you see.

For a long time, dental care has asked patients to trust without seeing. The dentist looks. The dentist explains. You nod and hope you understood. That can leave you feeling uncertain about decisions that affect your health.

We wanted something different.

Now, we can pull up your scans and walk through them with you. The wear pattern that points to nighttime clenching. The shift in your bite over time. The early signs that one tooth is starting to affect another.

Everything is digital and saved, so each visit builds on the last. We can compare year over year — celebrating progress, catching changes before they become problems.

That kind of clarity changes how care feels. You're not just being told what to do. You're seeing why, and choosing alongside us.

This is what transparent dentistry actually looks like.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNLD8iYg--rGD1Hz7qy3VPwHDXqZ1RcFM-2RNU=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://gangerfamilydentistry.digitalfloss.com/learnmore", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-05-06T19:22:19", "expires_at": "2026-11-05T19:22:19", "promo_code": null}]

description: Aspen Dental in Chicago, IL - South Loop makes dental care simple, clear, and easy to access for patients in Printer’s Row, Museum Campus, Dearborn Park, and Central Station communities. Led by practice owner Abigail Gloria Brier, our team provides dental exams, cleanings, fillings, crowns, tooth extractions, dentures, dental implants and emergency dental services. Conveniently located near Roosevelt Road and State Street, close to Grant Park and the Field Museum of Natural History, we focus on clear conversations, comfortable visits and care plans built just for you. New patients and walk-ins welcome. Most dental insurance plans accepted. We do not accept Medicaid. We offer flexible third-party financing options to fit your budget.

[{"id": "7230109504110049897", "text": "A Healthy Aging Check-In

Healthy Aging Month is a good reminder that changes in the mouth can reveal when an older loved one may need extra support. Use the M.O.U.T.H. checklist:

M — Meals: Are they avoiding certain foods, chewing on one side or taking longer to eat?

O — Ongoing symptoms: Watch for bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, sores, swelling or dry mouth.

U — Unusual behavior: Are they speaking less, resisting brushing or avoiding smiling and socializing?

T — Teeth and dentures: Look for loose or painful teeth, or dentures that click, slip, crack or cause sore spots.

H — Health and medications: Note changes in overall health, medications, memory, mobility or blood glucose.

If something seems different, the team at Aspen Dental can help identify the cause and recommend the right next step.

We offer a comprehensive range of general and advanced specialty areas including Endodontists (root canal), Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, Oral Medicine & Facial Pain (TMJ) specialists, Orthodontists (braces), Pediatric and Special Needs Dentists, Periodontists (gum disease) and Prosthodontists (implants, restorations). description: For over 100 years, we have provided the widest range of general and specialty dental care services for adults and children in Chicago – all in one place. Our faculty, students and staff are dedicated to educating and helping you make the best decisions to maintain good oral health. We offer a comprehensive range of general and advanced specialty areas including Endodontists (root canal), Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, Oral Medicine & Facial Pain (TMJ) specialists, Orthodontists (braces), Pediatric and Special Needs Dentists, Periodontists (gum disease) and Prosthodontists (implants, restorations). Our 40+ researchers are advancing scientific knowledge to transform oral health for communities across the world.

description: For over 100 years, we have provided the widest range of general and specialty dental care services for adults and children in Chicago – all in one place. Our faculty, students and staff are dedicated to educating and helping you make the best decisions to maintain good oral health. We offer a comprehensive range of general and advanced specialty areas including Endodontists (root canal), Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, Oral Medicine & Facial Pain (TMJ) specialists, Orthodontists (braces), Pediatric and Special Needs Dentists, Periodontists (gum disease) and Prosthodontists (implants, restorations). Our 40+ researchers are advancing scientific knowledge to transform oral health for communities across the world.

description: For over 100 years, we have provided the widest range of general and specialty dental care services for adults and children in Chicago – all in one place. description: Do you enjoy taking your child to the dentist? At Chicago Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics, we believe that the dental experience doesn’t have to be a scary one for children and teens or a stressful one for parents. Our friendly team members go above and beyond to help everyone feel relaxed and welcome. We have equipped our office with advanced technology, including soft tissue lasers, digital impression scanners, 3D printers, and much more to help our young patients feel comfortable during diagnosis and treatment. At Archer Dentistry, our expert team performs root canals to save damaged or infected teeth and prevent extraction. This treatment removes the inflamed pulp from inside the tooth, alleviating pain and protecting your natural tooth.

Watch for signs like persistent tooth pain, sensitivity, or swelling—these could indicate the need for a root canal. Our painless, multi-step procedure involves cleaning and sealing the tooth, with restoration options like fillings or crowns afterward.

Root canals are always better than extractions, as they allow you to keep your natural tooth, preserving your smile and long-term oral health.

Need root canal treatment in Chicago? Call Archer Dentistry today to book your appointment!

For more information about Root Canals, take a look at our blog post!

Teeth cleanings are essential for maintaining good oral and physical health. At Archer Dentistry, our professional cleanings remove plaque and tartar buildup, preventing gum disease, cavities, and bad breath. Regular cleanings are especially important for those prone to gum disease, with visits recommended every 3-4 months, while others may only need bi-annual cleanings.

During the cleaning, our team uses advanced tools to thoroughly remove plaque, followed by polishing to keep your teeth clean and healthy. After the procedure, you may experience temporary sensitivity, but this will subside quickly.

Delaying cleanings can lead to serious issues like tooth loss due to advanced gum disease. But don’t worry—regular cleanings by our skilled dentists will protect your smile without damaging your teeth!

Ready to schedule your next cleaning? Call Archer Dentistry today to book your appointment! For more information regarding Cleanings, take a look at our recent blog post!

[{"id": "2974276970998915463", "text": "Preventive dentistry helps patients protect their teeth and gums through childhood, adulthood, and the golden years of life. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMJMmZCTXtrJSrd5mmdD-m2Szbv0dhAFqZBr-j9=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/preventive-dentistry-preserving-your-smile-through-every-stage-of-life/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-03T02:47:16", "expires_at": "2027-03-05T02:47:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6139055585773361918", "text": "While there are several ways to improve your smile, dental veneers are a popular and effective option to brighten and balance your teeth. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPSY0etBfcTa3-edE7_S80TmO7kOrvvYMYFPctS=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/are-dental-veneers-right-for-me/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-08-13T15:52:09", "expires_at": "2027-02-12T15:52:07", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "258480071169474755", "text": "If your dental restorations feel off, do not wait to seek professional assistance. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNBaYoDLtIvw8dP9wK7OibnNBXGwZ8jGzmlXI9P=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/repair-a-damaged-restoration-with-a-restorative-dentist-near-me/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-07-22T11:42:08", "expires_at": "2027-01-21T11:42:07", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2602593800706687087", "text": "A family dentist identifies the cause of white spots on the enamel and suggests the best way to restore the smile to a healthy, even glow. These marks often appear chalky or pale compared to the rest of the tooth and sometimes signal that the outer layer is weakening.  

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPRMoJH41OYJwnmE1KTUJ4GuVAZE1GX6lwyhL6R=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/white-spots-on-your-teeth-get-help-from-a-family-dentist/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-06-05T18:15:25", "expires_at": "2026-12-05T18:15:23", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3865391214267695542", "text": "When you experience a chipped tooth, consulting a cosmetic dentist is the most effective way to restore your smile to its full health and beauty. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMDJHurgfW0mwkJHFZ_8z4zcg4XZifCt66XWhLv=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/chipped-tooth-treatment-options-from-a-cosmetic-dentist/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-05-05T00:37:16", "expires_at": "2026-11-04T00:37:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1356048603754279929", "text": "The best way to stop oral cancer is by undergoing regular oral cancer screening during dental checkups. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMwZsdOLu-34lI8ABMf4Ew6BNF9uqEOsCslTWuq=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/should-i-get-an-oral-cancer-screening/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-04-20T12:40:15", "expires_at": "2026-10-20T12:40:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3973609348332610213", "text": "After a tooth extraction, restoring function and appearance is a priority to maintain your oral health. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMqyeOeIbCS36AMl1glETIulRfMowx8r1aNrTQJ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/tooth-replacement-options-after-a-tooth-extraction/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-03-17T21:29:28", "expires_at": "2026-09-16T21:29:27", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3052247187236373686", "text": "All-on-4 implant treatment has become a transformative option for individuals seeking full-arch restoration, and understanding several important factors before choosing all-on-4 is essential. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipO7lqe78-0tXwalXwse-_uycm7y35Y28jPqieSS=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/factors-to-consider-before-getting-all-on-4-implants/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-02-19T18:06:10", "expires_at": "2026-08-21T18:06:08", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6220783384770744623", "text": "A dental bridge is often an important tooth-replacement option when one or more teeth are missing in the same area. 

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPI5QN__C-g2Top8o1dNlkSCH0Y3KseNNgpxH2r=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://smilestudiochicago.com/blog/tooth-replacement-101-why-a-dentist-may-recommend-a-dental-bridge/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-01-20T17:33:07", "expires_at": "2026-07-22T17:33:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1586013402638315084", "text": "Denture repair is a common need for patients who wear partial or full dentures. While these oral appliances are strong, they are prone to breaking because of their delicacy.

[{"id": "2546828206149248839", "text": "🦷✨ Why Do My Teeth Look Yellow?
Teeth can naturally become less bright over time, and several factors can contribute to a yellow appearance. Coffee, tea, red wine, tobacco, and certain foods can cause surface staining. ☕🍷🚬 As enamel becomes thinner with age, the naturally yellowish dentin underneath may also become more visible.

Good brushing and regular professional cleanings can help remove surface stains. 🪥✨ If you’re considering whitening, talk with our dentist first to determine which option is safe and appropriate for your smile. 😊💙", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMQDLY3BzZIskXhwa6dFtJRNHX9PEKJ7zhkw5F1=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-19T02:43:59", "expires_at": "2027-03-21T02:43:58", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "57523350899373499", "text": "✨ Tooth bonding can be a simple, conservative option for repairing minor dental imperfections. 🦷

Using tooth-colored composite material, our dentist can reshape or restore areas affected by small chips, discoloration, gaps, or minor wear. 💫 The material is carefully matched to your natural tooth color and bonded to the tooth for a seamless appearance.

⏱️ Treatment is often completed in a single visit.

[{"id": "8380224376850791408", "text": "Our Chicago Loop functional dentist office goes beyond traditional dental care — we take a comprehensive approach to improving oral and overall health.

Functional dentistry focuses on the connection between oral health and the rest of your body. By addressing underlying issues such as sleep apnea, teeth clenching, and mouth breathing, we aim to enhance your well-being through holistic treatment.

At Choices in Dentistry, we recognize the profound impact of oral health on overall health and are here to help you achieve optimal wellness.", "type": "event", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNCCjtg9Ptxg0CKC9bAjG4I9MJOujFVus6NlO7k=h400-no", "title": "Go Beyond Traditional Dentistry for a Healthier You!", "cta_url": "https://choicesindentistry.com/functional-dentistry/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-16T20:36:22", "expires_at": "2025-10-30T04:59:59", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8187558917819076128", "text": "When you hold your teeth together too often, you can create pain in the joint that opens and closes your mouth. This is the temporomandibular joint, more commonly known as the TMJ. Inflammation of the TMJ is the cause of pain and stiffness in the jaw joint.

So, how does the TMJ become inflamed?

Believe it or not, teeth clenching or grinding is the most common cause of TMJ inflammation and pain.

What most people do not realize is that ANY contact between teeth other than when eating is too much contact. At rest, there is supposed to be a space between your teeth. When you ask someone to close their lips, they should not automatically touch their teeth. Teeth that touch are a stress on the TMJ and lead to inflammation and pain.

At Choices in Dentistry, we offer our patients non-surgical TMJ treatments that really work.", "type": "event", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNdZohaHN0flGh3yWw40qYmJ0lUfzOPhOR2ove8=h400-no", "title": "Ready to Stop Your TMJ Pain Without Surgery?", "cta_url": "https://choicesindentistry.com/tmj-treatment/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-16T20:31:11", "expires_at": "2025-10-28T04:59:59", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8285129362100859399", "text": "Ozone conjures up thoughts of global warming holding in greenhouse gases. But remember the ozone isn’t the problem— the ozone protects us from UV radiation that causes skin cancers. Ozone is beneficial in many other ways, too.

Time for a little science. Ozone is made by forcing an additional atom of oxygen onto O2, the oxygen we breathe. This forced third oxygen atom is fragile. It wants to break loose. When it does, the environment “rebalances” and makes a highly effective antioxidant. Get it? Even our bodies produce ozone at the white cell level to kill offending microorganisms. What could be more natural?

This antioxidant will kill off bacteria, viruses, and fungi, rebalancing your biofilm when treating cavities, gum disease, root canals, canker sores, and more. Here at Choices in Dentistry, we use ozone therapy to keep your bacterial pathogens in balance to treat cavities, gum disease, and therefore improve overall health.

Dental ozone therapy is part of our integrative focus and by offering something not seen at traditional offices to improve your health.", "type": "event", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipP1OONBKwP-z1LsJrA8or-hTiEf6Bi8TT9XL2GS=h400-no", "title": "What Is Ozone Therapy in Dentistry?", "cta_url": "https://choicesindentistry.com/ozone-therapy/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-09T19:16:57", "expires_at": "2025-10-18T04:59:59", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2592009033391959148", "text": "This question should be discussed from the perspective of your systemic health AND your dental health. 

Systemically, everyone is different. One person could have multiple fillings and no problems. Others may have a small single filling and having a strong reaction to it. So the quantity of mercury doesn’t matter — your immune response matters. 

Symptoms that could be attributed to silver mercury fillings include:

- Irritability
- Fatigue

[{"id": "4360634938804193432", "text": "Broken or Damaged Tooth? When Might You Need a Same-Day Crown?

A cracked or broken tooth can happen suddenly, sometimes from biting something hard or because an old filling has weakened the tooth.

In many cases, the tooth may still be restored with a crown instead of being removed.

A same-day crown may be considered if:

• Part of the tooth has broken off
• A large filling has weakened the tooth
• The tooth is cracked or badly worn
• The tooth needs extra protection after treatment

If enough healthy tooth structure remains, your dentist may be able to design and place the crown during the same visit.

Not every damaged tooth is suitable for a same-day crown, so an examination is important before treatment is recommended.

Contact our dental team to have your tooth checked and discuss whether a same-day crown may be right for you.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPCX27qylzlB2SCBhIPiERDTB6lsVNuwtRGU2JZ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-03T05:30:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-03T11:21:10", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "4400852150169620709", "text": "Dental bonding vs veneers: which option is right for your smile?

Both treatments can improve the look of chipped, stained, uneven, or slightly gapped teeth, but they are not the same. Dental bonding is often used for smaller cosmetic fixes, while veneers may be recommended for a more complete smile transformation.

Dental bonding may help with:

• Small chips or cracks
• Minor gaps between teeth
• Slight tooth reshaping
• Small areas of discoloration
• A more conservative cosmetic option

Veneers may help with:

• Multiple visible smile concerns
• Stubborn stains that do not respond to whitening
• Worn, uneven, or misshapen teeth
• A longer-lasting smile makeover option
• A more uniform smile appearance

The right choice depends on your tooth condition, smile goals, budget, and oral health. A dental evaluation can help you compare both options and choose the treatment that fits your smile best.

Schedule your cosmetic dentistry consultation today.

Yes, Invisalign may help many adults improve mild to moderate crowding, crooked teeth, gaps, and alignment concerns without traditional metal braces. These clear aligners are removable, discreet, and designed to gradually move teeth into better positions.

Invisalign may be a good option if you have:

• Crowded front teeth
• Crooked or overlapping teeth
• Small gaps between teeth
• Teeth that shifted after braces
• Mild bite alignment concerns
• A desire for a more discreet orthodontic option

However, not every case is the same. Severe crowding, complex bite problems, or gum health concerns may require a different treatment plan. A dental evaluation can help determine whether Invisalign is suitable for your smile goals.

Our El Paso dental team can examine your teeth, review your bite, and explain your clear aligner options.

Schedule your Invisalign consultation today.

Could Teeth Grinding Be the Cause?

Many people clench or grind their teeth at night without knowing it. 
Over time, this pressure can affect your teeth, jaw muscles, and bite.

Common signs of teeth grinding may include:

• Morning jaw pain or tightness
• Frequent headaches
• Tooth sensitivity
• Worn, chipped, or cracked teeth
• Sore facial muscles
• Pain when chewing
• Clicking or discomfort in the jaw

A custom nightguard may help protect your teeth from grinding damage and reduce pressure on the jaw while you sleep. Your dentist can check for signs of bruxism and recommend the right option based on your symptoms.

Do not ignore ongoing jaw pain or morning headaches. Early care can help protect your smile and prevent further tooth damage.

Schedule a teeth grinding evaluation today.

[{"id": "3061434579643754168", "text": "Self-care has become a widely discussed concept, and for good reason — the demands of modern life are real, and taking deliberate time to invest in your own health and wellbeing matters. But self-care doesn't have to mean elaborate routines or significant expense. Sometimes it's as simple as booking an appointment you've been putting off.


A professional dental cleaning is, genuinely, one of the most effective things you can do for yourself in under an hour. Your hygienist removes buildup that brushing and flossing can't address, polishes away surface stains that have accumulated over months, and checks for early signs of issues that are far easier to manage now than later. You leave feeling cleaner, fresher, and with the quiet satisfaction of having done something concretely good for your health.


There's also the confidence factor. A clean, healthy smile affects how you feel in social and professional situations — it's one of the first things people notice, and taking care of it is a form of self-respect that pays dividends in ways that are hard to quantify but easy to feel.


If you've been running on fumes and putting everyone else's needs ahead of your own, this is your reminder that your health belongs on the priority list too. You can't pour from an empty cup, as the saying goes — and you can't flash a confident smile if you've been neglecting the thing that makes it possible.


Book the cleaning. You've earned it.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPcymIX4NdOm0SiezeQvmTlUMlV8VNH7np2VAKP=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-18T23:00:42", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T23:00:40", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1293393192352264113", "text": "The relationship between oral health and overall health is one of the most important — and most underappreciated — connections in medicine. For decades, dentistry and medicine operated largely in separate silos. That's changing, and the research behind the shift is compelling.


Gum disease, in particular, has been linked to a range of serious systemic conditions. The bacteria associated with periodontal infections can enter the bloodstream through inflamed gum tissue, triggering inflammatory responses throughout the body. Studies have found associations between gum disease and cardiovascular disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, respiratory conditions, and adverse pregnancy outcomes including premature birth and low birth weight.


The relationship with diabetes is especially well established and runs in both directions. People with diabetes are more susceptible to gum disease due to impaired immune response and reduced ability to fight infection. And gum disease, in turn, can make blood sugar harder to control — creating a cycle that worsens both conditions simultaneously.


None of this is meant to be alarming. It's meant to reframe how you think about dental care. A dental visit isn't just about your teeth — it's a meaningful investment in your cardiovascular health, your metabolic health, and your overall wellbeing. Your dentist and your physician are, in a very real sense, working toward the same goal.


Take care of your gums. The rest of your body is paying attention.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOhErftamEdsLVBmnX9T_lVnooMALuPQRc9FkOd=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-11T23:12:09", "expires_at": "2027-03-13T23:12:07", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3667600773968541744", "text": "Oral health doesn't look the same at every stage of life — and for older adults, the risks and considerations shift in ways that are worth understanding. September is a good time to think about the dental health of the seniors in your life, whether that's a parent, grandparent, or yourself.

Dry mouth is one of the most common oral health challenges for older adults, and it's frequently a side effect of medications rather than aging itself. Hundreds of commonly prescribed drugs — including those for blood pressure, depression, allergies, and pain — list dry mouth as a side effect. Since saliva is the mouth's primary defense against bacteria and acid, chronically reduced saliva flow significantly increases the risk of cavities and gum disease, even in people who have maintained good oral hygiene for decades.

Gum disease is also more prevalent and more aggressive in older adults, partly due to immune system changes and partly due to accumulated exposure over time. It's the leading cause of tooth loss in adults, and tooth loss has its own downstream effects on nutrition, speech, confidence, and quality of life.

Regular dental visits are important at every age, but they're especially critical for seniors whose oral health landscape is shifting. If an older person in your life has been avoiding the dentist — whether due to cost, mobility, anxiety, or simply not prioritizing it — this is a gentle nudge to help them get back on track.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOyCWcNIiqCZDI9MIa0wHP0erq6aoqPQjrrqyY1=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-04T23:04:46", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T23:04:44", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8333109394098020347", "text": "September is just around the corner, and with it comes that familiar shift in pace — school routines, work schedules, and the general acceleration that carries most people straight through to the holidays before they know it. Before that happens, it's worth taking a moment to reset your oral health routine and make sure you're heading into the busier months in good shape.

Think of late August as a natural checkpoint. Have you had both of your cleanings this year? Is there any treatment your dentist has recommended that you've been putting off? Are your kids up to date on their checkups? These are easy things to let slide when life gets busy, and the fall season has a way of making everything feel more urgent and compressed.

Getting ahead of it now — before the holidays arrive and schedules become nearly impossible — means you're not scrambling in November or December trying to squeeze in appointments before the year ends and benefits reset. It also means that if any treatment is recommended, you have time to get it done while your benefits are still available.

The connection between routine and oral health is real. People who maintain consistent dental habits and keep their scheduled appointments tend to have significantly fewer and less complex dental issues over time. It's not complicated — it's just consistency.

Use this seasonal transition as your cue. A quick call to schedule your fall appointment today means one less thing to think about when September hits.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMGJA1gLjL4VHTQGYeifyATxD7fGE91VFfTINO-=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-28T23:03:27", "expires_at": "2027-02-27T23:03:25", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2494821960813418192", "text": "If you have teenagers, you're probably already aware of how central energy drinks and sports drinks have become to their daily routines. What you may not realize is just how damaging those beverages can be to their teeth — and how quickly the damage can accumulate.

The problem is twofold. Most energy drinks and sports drinks contain significant amounts of sugar, which feeds the bacteria that produce cavity-causing acid. But even the sugar-free versions are typically highly acidic on their own — with pH levels low enough to directly erode tooth enamel with repeated exposure. Enamel erosion is permanent. Once that protective outer layer is worn away, it cannot regenerate.

Teenagers are particularly vulnerable because their enamel is still maturing, and because consumption patterns tend to be high — sipping throughout the day rather than having a drink with a meal and moving on. That sustained, repeated acid exposure is far more damaging than occasional consumption would be.

The conversation worth having isn't necessarily about eliminating these drinks entirely — that's a difficult sell with most teenagers. It's about frequency and habits. Drinking through a straw reduces direct contact with teeth. Rinsing with water afterward helps neutralize acid. And avoiding these drinks as an all-day sipping habit is probably the most impactful change of all.

Bring it up at their next dental visit. Sometimes hearing it from the dentist lands differently than hearing it from a parent.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNHPhZdVDMYbWo0cD2FaK-TN0Two7GntZRGeiel=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-21T23:37:58", "expires_at": "2027-02-20T23:37:56", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3511690590271506569", "text": "A new school year is a natural reset point — new teachers, new supplies, new routines. It's also a great opportunity to revisit your child's oral health habits and make sure the basics are actually happening the way they should be.

Brushing twice a day for two full minutes is the foundation. Two minutes sounds simple, but most kids — and plenty of adults — fall well short of it without realizing. The easiest fix is a timer. A two-minute sand timer kept on the bathroom counter, a brushing app on a phone or tablet, or simply playing a favorite two-minute song can make the habit more engaging and ensure the time is actually being met.

Technique matters too. Many kids brush in fast, haphazard strokes that miss large areas entirely. Gentle, circular motions across all surfaces — outer, inner, and chewing — cover the mouth much more effectively. Make sure they're brushing their tongue as well, which harbors a significant amount of bacteria.

Flossing is equally important and even more commonly skipped. Once teeth are touching, a toothbrush simply cannot clean between them. Floss picks can be easier for kids to manage than traditional floss, and building it into the nighttime routine early makes it far more likely to stick as a lifelong habit.

Take a few minutes this week to brush alongside your kids and make sure their technique is where it should be. The habits they build now will serve them for decades.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNOaXPkUdvjb8_oTCDOnLCZ97LHtdAHbyepgjiz=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-14T04:00:38", "expires_at": "2027-02-13T04:00:36", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5825086246610208994", "text": "Here's a fact that surprises a lot of parents: tooth decay is one of the most prevalent chronic diseases among children in the United States — more common than asthma, more common than diabetes. And yet it's almost entirely preventable with the right habits and regular professional care.
Cavities don't just cause pain. They affect eating, sleeping, speaking, and concentrating. Children with untreated tooth decay miss more school, perform worse academically, and experience more disruption to their daily lives than kids whose dental health is being properly managed. The impact goes well beyond the mouth.

The encouraging part is that prevention is genuinely straightforward. Twice-daily brushing with fluoride toothpaste, daily flossing, limiting sugary snacks and beverages, drinking fluoridated water, and seeing a dentist every six months — these habits, practiced consistently, dramatically reduce a child's risk of developing cavities.

Dental sealants are another highly effective preventive tool. Applied to the chewing surfaces of back teeth, sealants create a barrier that prevents bacteria and food particles from settling into the grooves where cavities most commonly form. They're quick, painless, and can last for years.

If your child is due for a checkup, don't wait. And if cavities have been a recurring issue, ask your dentist about sealants and other preventive options. Keeping kids in the classroom starts with keeping them healthy.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNY7Atd1m3p_cE-05bfPrDxrWB4Soduy_HBGL5J=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-07T23:22:43", "expires_at": "2027-02-06T23:22:42", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3999597480555467392", "text": "Back to school season has a way of sneaking up fast. One minute it's the Fourth of July, and the next you're scrambling for school supplies, new shoes, and a hundred other things on the list. Before the chaos of a new school year fully takes over, there's one appointment worth getting on the calendar early — the kids' dental checkup. 


Late summer is one of the busiest times of year for pediatric dental appointments, which means if you wait too long, you'll be competing with every other family who had the same idea in August. Getting ahead of it now — while there's still flexibility in the schedule — means less stress and more appointment availability.

Beyond the logistics, there's a real health reason to prioritize it. Cavities are one of the most common chronic conditions among school-age children, and untreated tooth pain is a documented cause of missed school days and difficulty concentrating in class. A child dealing with dental discomfort isn't able to focus the way they should be. Addressing any issues before the school year starts means they're walking in on day one feeling their best.

If your child is starting at a new school this year, some programs also require proof of a recent dental exam. Check the requirements early so you're not caught off guard.

Add it to the back to school list. It's one of the most important items on it.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMIJpUZnvNCqj4LRVGJ9zr3TCNegE-V-9zAolzh=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-07-31T23:45:47", "expires_at": "2027-01-30T23:45:46", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5946358202326001554", "text": "Summer snacking is real — and between the heat, the activities, and the general abundance of treats at every backyard gathering, it's easy to fall into patterns that aren't great for your teeth. The good news is that a few simple swaps can make a meaningful difference without taking any of the fun out of the season.


The biggest issue with most popular snacks isn't just sugar — it's texture and frequency. Sticky snacks like fruit snacks, gummy candies, and granola bars cling to tooth surfaces and sit in the grooves of molars long after you've finished eating. Frequent snacking throughout the day means your teeth are under near-continuous acid attack, since oral bacteria produce acid every time they process sugar or refined carbohydrates.


Crunchy fruits and vegetables — apples, carrots, celery, cucumber — are genuinely great for your teeth. Their texture stimulates saliva production, helps scrub tooth surfaces, and most contain a high percentage of water. Cheese is another surprisingly tooth-friendly snack, as it's low in sugar, high in calcium, and helps neutralize acid in the mouth.


You don't have to give up summer treats entirely. Just be mindful of frequency — try to have sweets at mealtimes rather than throughout the day, and follow up with water.


Snack smart this summer. Your teeth are paying attention even when you're not.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPPWJEBkUDZ2Df6g8dw_bc5omET3y61_QmGJqZv=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-07-24T23:05:12", "expires_at": "2027-01-23T23:05:11", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6943622372894434990", "text": "Summer sports season is in full swing, and whether your kids are playing soccer, baseball, basketball, football, or any other contact or semi-contact activity, there's one piece of protective gear that's consistently overlooked — the mouthguard.


Dental injuries are among the most common sports injuries in children and adolescents. A single collision, fall, or errant elbow can result in a chipped, cracked, or knocked-out tooth — and depending on the tooth and the severity of the injury, the treatment can be complex, lengthy, and expensive. The American Dental Association estimates that mouthguards prevent hundreds of thousands of dental injuries every year.


The stock mouthguards available at sporting goods stores offer some protection, but a custom-fitted mouthguard made by your dentist offers significantly better fit, comfort, and coverage. A guard that fits properly is more likely to actually be worn — kids are far less likely to remove or avoid a guard that doesn't feel bulky or uncomfortable.


If your child is active in sports this summer and doesn't have a mouthguard, or is using a store-bought one that they complain about constantly, it's worth having a conversation with your dentist about a custom option. It's one of the most cost-effective preventive investments you can make.
